purpose: Track where Jamie's contribution is established, where role-specific collaborator evidence would make it stronger, and how to narrow the claim if that evidence is not recovered.

established: Public records establish that NYC Artist Coalition existed, convened artists and cultural-space stakeholders, and entered official cultural-policy and Council records.
Jamie's first-person account identifies an instrumental role in facilitating the coalition's formation.
neededEvidence: A role-specific account from a founding collaborator describing what Jamie initiated, facilitated, or maintained.
A dated formation artifact that connects Jamie to the first convening or operating workflow.
confirmAction: Invite one or more founding collaborators to review a short, bounded role statement and suggest corrections.
Preserve any response as collaborator-provided evidence with date, permission, and quotation boundaries.
narrowAction: Until corroborated, describe Jamie as an active coalition contributor who built campaign, event, documentation, and digital systems rather than as sole founder.
Keep formation language attributed to Jamie's memory.

items.project: NYC Artist Coalition campaign and event systems
established: Public campaign sites, event records, social records, and Council materials establish a sustained system of convenings and issue campaigns.
The archive supports Jamie's role in web production, public information systems, testimony, facilitation, and operating continuity.
neededEvidence: Collaborator accounts distinguishing Jamie's event-production, facilitation, publishing, and campaign-infrastructure responsibilities from shared coalition work.
Contemporaneous run-of-show, assignment, or launch artifacts with public-safe role attribution.
confirmAction: Ask recurring collaborators to review one campaign at a time rather than requesting a global endorsement.
Record both confirming and limiting recollections.
narrowAction: Use contributed, produced, facilitated, built, and maintained for evidenced tasks.
Do not convert shared-account output into sole authorship.

established: Official records establish the Cabaret Law repeal and MARCH reporting legislation as institutional outcomes.
Official hearing records establish Council use of coalition testimony and research.
neededEvidence: Role-specific accounts from coalition and government collaborators connecting Jamie's contribution to particular decision inputs without assigning sole causality.
Additional records that show how findings, events, testimony, or campaign artifacts moved into legislative work.
confirmAction: Seek bounded descriptions of which contribution was useful, to whom, and at what decision point.
Keep outcome evidence and contribution evidence separately cited.
narrowAction: Say Jamie contributed to coalition advocacy that informed or supported the outcome.
Do not say Jamie caused passage, created an office alone, or secured an institutional decision.

items.project: WOWList product, publishing, and community operations
established: Code, database, public-web, and social archives establish the platform's product surface and operating scale.
Jamie and Richard Caceres are credited as collaborators; Jamie's memory says he managed the project's social presence.
neededEvidence: Richard Caceres's account of role division across product, engineering, publishing, onboarding, and community support.
Organizer accounts describing how they used the platform and what Jamie's support enabled.
confirmAction: Invite Richard to annotate a concise responsibility matrix.
Seek two user-side accounts from different city ecosystems.
narrowAction: Continue to say co-built and distinguish platform records from individual authorship.
Treat social-account authorship as unresolved unless a record or collaborator resolves it.

established: Jamie confirms that he hosts Sunday Dinner.
Public sources corroborate a recurring open hosting form and the current public project surface.
neededEvidence: Participant or co-host accounts describing the hosting, onboarding, facilitation, and continuity work Jamie performed.
A privacy-preserving method note for the gathering and resident-artist aggregates.
confirmAction: Invite a small, diverse set of participants to review a bounded description without publishing guest history.
Reconcile aggregate counts privately and publish only the resulting method note.
narrowAction: Keep 300+ gatherings and 20+ resident artists marked careful until the metric method is documented.
Never publish attendance records, addresses, guest lists, or private messages.

items.project: KC Town Hall phase one field coordination
established: The successful public-benefit proposal documents phase-one scope and completed work.
Jamie's first-person account describes daily general-contractor coordination and the neighborhood survey system.
neededEvidence: A project collaborator, architect, engineer, or trade partner account confirming Jamie's coordination role and scope.
Public-safe dated artifacts connecting Jamie to phase-one sequencing and field decisions.
confirmAction: Seek one owner-side and one delivery-side role confirmation.
Keep the later project transition separate from phase-one completion.
narrowAction: Use served as general contractor for phase one only when corroboration is attached; otherwise say coordinated phase-one field delivery.
Do not imply completion of the full adaptive-reuse project.

established: Public campaign materials establish the fund and named organizers.
An AI-assisted archival review supports Jamie's behind-the-scenes web, theme, widget, and platform contribution.
neededEvidence: A named organizer's account confirming the specific digital responsibilities and useful result.
A public-safe code or launch artifact if a stronger public proof is needed.
confirmAction: Ask a named organizer to correct a short technical-support statement.
Identify any response as collaborator testimony rather than retroactively attributing the AI review.
narrowAction: Keep the claim as behind-the-scenes digital infrastructure.
Do not call Jamie an organizer, grant decision-maker, fiscal sponsor, or fundraiser owner.
